title: Sparse neighbour constraints
spec: Instead of all n(n-1)/2 pair constraints, include only pairs whose centres are closer than a cutoff (for example r_i + r_j + 0.2 at the start point), rebuilt every few SLSQP restarts or after each solve. Keep the boundary and radius constraints. This shrinks the constraint matrix so SLSQP runs faster, and a final check ensures no excluded pair overlaps, re-solving if it does.

title: Quasi-random Halton starting centres
spec: Draw the initial centres from a scrambled Halton sequence (bases 2 and 3, scrambled with a permutation drawn from rng) mapped into [0.05, 0.95]^2, instead of uniform random points. Keep the equal-radius phase 1 and the free SLSQP phase 2 unchanged. The aim is more uniform coverage of the square at the start, so different restarts explore different basins.

title: Alternating block optimisation of centres and radii
spec: Replace the joint SLSQP with alternating block coordinate ascent. Step A: fix the radii and maximise the minimum slack over the centres (a minimax problem, solved by SLSQP over centres and one epigraph variable). Step B: fix the centres and solve the radius LP with linprog to maximise sum(r). Repeat A and B for up to 15 rounds, or until the gain in sum(r) falls below 1e-9. Use the original joint SLSQP only as a final polish. Each block is smaller and better conditioned than the full problem, so the alternation may escape the basins that a joint solver settles into.

title: Corner-anchored restarts
spec: On each restart, with probability 0.5, pin four circles at the corners of the square. Their radii are fixed at a random value in [0.05, 0.2] and their centres are removed from the free variables. Initialise the other n-4 circles uniformly, then run the existing two-phase SLSQP on the free variables only, adding the fixed circles' constraints as constants. Repair and select as before. The point is to test whether corner-anchored basins are a different family from the free-start basins.

title: Greedy coordinate radius growth post-pass
spec: After the repair step, run a final pass with no SLSQP: visit the circles in a random order drawn from rng, and for each circle set its radius to the largest value allowed by the walls and its current neighbours, leaving the other circles fixed. Repeat the pass until no radius changes by more than 1e-12. The result is still valid by construction and can only increase the radius sum. Apply the pass to the best packing only.

title: Lloyd-relaxed centroidal Voronoi starts
spec: Generate the initial centres by Lloyd relaxation rather than uniform sampling. Draw about 4n random points in the square, assign each to its nearest of n seed centres, and move each seed to the centroid of its cell. Repeat 20 iterations, which yields an approximately centroidal, evenly spread layout. Add small uniform jitter of 0.02, clip to [0.05, 0.95], and then run the existing two-phase SLSQP. This gives well-spread starts whose cells are roughly equal, instead of the random layouts the restarts draw now.

title: Soft-mode perturbation of the incumbent
spec: After a local solve, build the Hessian-like matrix J^T J over the active pair and wall constraints at the optimum, where J is the Jacobian of the active constraints in the centre coordinates. Take the eigenvectors with the smallest nonzero eigenvalues (the softest modes of the packing). Perturb the incumbent by moving the centres along 1 to 3 of these modes with amplitude 0.02 to 0.05, scaled by a random sign, then re-run the two-phase SLSQP. Accept the result if it beats the incumbent. Soft modes are the directions in which the packing can rearrange most cheaply, so this is a more structured kick than isotropic noise.

title: Log-uniform kick radius with two timescales
spec: Replace the kick radius R = uniform(0.15, 0.35) by R = exp(uniform(log 0.04, log 0.5)), a log-uniform draw spanning small local shakes to large rearrangements. Use the same draw for the disc and the re-randomised points. Keep the rest of the walk unchanged. This tests whether the walk benefits from occasional very large kicks, which the current narrow range never produces, and it does not change the code size.

title: Record-to-record travel acceptance on the kick walk
spec: Change the acceptance rule of the disc re-randomisation walk. Keep a current packing cur that may differ from the best. After each kick and re-optimisation, accept the new packing if its sum of radii is at least best_sum minus a threshold T, where T starts at 0.02 and decreases linearly to 0 over the time budget. Always update best when the new sum exceeds it. This lets the walk drift across shallow basins early on and tighten up late, unlike the current strict-improvement rule. No other change.

title: Kick-centre placement at the largest empty hole
spec: Choose the kick centre p not uniformly at random but at the largest empty circle of the incumbent. Sample 2000 random points in the square, compute each point's distance to the nearest circle boundary, and set p to the point with the largest clearance (with a random tie-break). With probability 0.3 keep the uniform random centre to preserve diversity. The kick radius R and the disc re-randomisation stay as in the current code. This concentrates perturbation in the packing's loosest region, where a radius gain is most likely.

title: Racing of candidate kicks
spec: At each walk step, generate K=4 candidate kicks from the incumbent, each with its own random centre and radius. Run a cheap SLSQP (MAX_ITER=30) on each candidate. Keep the best two after this short stage and run the full _solve_once on those two only, taking the better result as the new candidate. This spends the expensive phase-2 time on the most promising kicks, instead of one kick per step. The time budget is still checked against process_time between steps.

title: Slack-proportional per-circle kicks
spec: After each local solve, compute for each circle its slack, defined as the minimum over its wall gaps and pair gaps of the distance minus the sum of radii. Set the kick amplitude for circle i to be proportional to its slack, with a floor of 0.005 and a cap of 0.05. Perturb the centres of the incumbent with these amplitudes and re-run the two-phase SLSQP. Circles with more free room move more, and tightly jammed circles move little. Accept only improvements. This replaces the uniform kick size with one that depends on the local state of each circle.

title: Solver portfolio per walk step
spec: Inside each kick step, run two local solvers from the same kicked configuration: the existing two-phase SLSQP and a cheap L-BFGS-B penalty descent (overlap penalty with weight 1e3, followed by a 30-iteration SLSQP on the free radii). Keep whichever repaired packing has the larger sum of radii. Both solvers use the same seeded kick, so only the local solver varies. This hedges against SLSQP getting trapped after a large kick, at about twice the cost per step.

title: Annealed radius-variance regulariser
spec: In phase 2, change the objective to -sum(r) + lambda * sum((r - mean(r))^2), where lambda starts at 0.05 and is multiplied by 0.5 after each SLSQP call in the walk. Set lambda to 0 for the final polish. This pushes the search through equal-radius-like basins, which helped in phase 1 (slot 8), and then releases the pressure. Use the analytic gradient of this term only if it is cheap, otherwise let SLSQP use finite differences.

title: Homothety kick
spec: Replace the disc re-randomisation kick with a scaling kick. Pick a random point p in [0,1]^2 and a random factor f in [0.9, 1.1]; map every centre c to p + f*(c - p), clip to [0,1], set the radii to zero for circles that end up outside the wall-limited region, and re-run the existing two-phase SLSQP. This moves all circles coherently rather than re-sampling a disc, so it reaches configurations that the local disc kick cannot.

title: Augmented Lagrangian for the free-radius phase
spec: Replace the phase-2 SLSQP with an augmented Lagrangian loop. Minimise -sum(r) + sum over constraints of (lambda_k * g_k + (mu/2) * min(0, g_k)^2) with L-BFGS-B, where g_k >= 0 are the pair, wall and radius constraints. After each inner solve, update lambda_k = max(0, lambda_k - mu * g_k) and increase mu by a factor of 3 up to a cap. Run 5 to 8 outer iterations, then do one short SLSQP polish from the result so the final point is feasible-tight. Use the analytic gradient of the penalty terms.

title: CMA-ES over centres with SLSQP refinement
spec: Add a global search stage before the kick walk. Run a basic CMA-ES (population about 4+3ln(2n), rank-mu covariance update, step size from the 1/5 rule) over the 2n centre coordinates. The fitness of a candidate is the sum of radii from an exact LP for the radii with centres fixed (scipy linprog, HiGHS) after a repair-style feasibility check. Run CMA-ES for about 25% of the budget, then hand its best centres to the existing SLSQP phase 2. Keep the kick walk for the remaining time.

title: Golden-angle sunflower starts
spec: For one start in every three restarts, place the n centres on a sunflower (Vogel) spiral: point k at radius sqrt((k+0.5)/n) times a half-width scale and angle k*pi*(3-sqrt(5)), mapped into the square with the centre at (0.5, 0.5), plus a small seeded random rotation and jitter of about 0.02. Clip into [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW] and feed the result through the same phase-1 and phase-2 SLSQP pipeline. The spiral start is a structurally different seed from uniform and lattice starts.

title: Incremental curriculum build
spec: For the first start, grow the packing from k=3 to n circles one at a time. At each size, insert the new circle at the point with the largest empty clearance (sampled from about 500 random candidates), then run a short SLSQP (maxiter about 30) on the full free-radius problem for the current k circles. Use the final k=n result as the start for the usual phase-2 SLSQP. Restarts and kicks stay as they are. The build is cheap because each stage has few constraints.

title: Rattler relocation into the largest hole
spec: After each local solve, identify rattlers: circles whose radius is within 1e-6 of their wall or pair limit has no contacts, meaning no active pair or wall constraint is within 1e-7. Remove all rattlers, and place each one at the grid point that maximises the distance to the nearest centre minus that centre's radius, using a 150 by 150 grid. Then re-run the two-phase SLSQP with the relocated circles as the starting point, and keep the result only if sum(r) improves. Rattlers waste area without adding to the sum, so moving them to holes can unlock slack for the rest of the packing.

title: Best-of-ensemble averaging of seeds
spec: Make each solve call run two independent streams from rng children (np.random.default_rng(seed).spawn(2)) with different start types (random and lattice) and return whichever packing has the larger sum. Since the grader averages three seeds, a diverse portfolio within one call reduces the chance that all restarts converge to the same weak basin.

title: Stagewise hierarchical packing by size class
spec: Split the n circles into two groups: a few large circles (about 20 percent) and the rest. Solve first for the large-circle layout only, using SLSQP with the large circles as the variables, and then add the small circles at random in the gaps and run SLSQP on all circles together. This decomposes the search so the large circles, which decide the overall structure, are settled first. Keep the best final packing after _repair, as in the current solver.

title: Gradient-free refinement after SLSQP
spec: After SLSQP and the repair, run a short Nelder-Mead or coordinate search on the radii alone with the centres fixed, only accepting moves that keep the packing valid. This is a cheap post-polish that squeezes out a little sum from each candidate. Keep it short so most of the budget still goes to restarts.

title: Contact-graph Newton polish of the final packing
spec: After SLSQP and before the final _repair, identify the active contacts: pairs whose gap is below 1e-7, and circles touching a wall within 1e-7. Treat these as equalities and solve the resulting system with a few Gauss-Newton steps on the centres and radii, leaving unknowns free only where the system is determined. Accept a step only if the sum of radii increases and the packing still passes the exact validity check. The gain is small, but it recovers digits lost to SLSQP's tolerance using a local, cheap step.

title: Adaptive restart time budgeting
spec: Measure the time taken by the first few restarts and their final sums. Use a fixed short budget per restart (for example the mean of the first three restart times times 1.5) and cap restarts so that at least five complete within the time limit. This makes the number of restarts depend on the actual per-restart cost on the grader instead of a fixed count, and avoids wasting the last partial restart.

title: Annealed pull toward a random anchor
spec: Add a quadratic regularisation term to the phase-1 objective that pulls every centre toward a random anchor point drawn from rng, with weight lambda that starts at 0.05 and decays linearly to 0 over the phase-1 iterations. The term spreads the circles out early, and as it fades the true radius-sum objective takes over. Phase 2 keeps the unregularised objective, so the final answer is still judged on the true sum of radii.

title: Vacancy-dislocation hexagonal seeds
spec: For a random start, build a hexagonal lattice of roughly n+3 sites, scaled so that its row spacing fits the unit square with margin 0.1, choose a random row count between 5 and 7, then remove 3 random sites and insert a random dislocation by shifting one row by half a spacing. Keep n sites, jitter by 0.01, and pass them to the existing equal-radius phase 1 as the initial centres. Restarts alternate between this seed and the uniform random seed to diversify the basin set.

title: Container-scaling continuation
spec: Before the free-radius solve, run one extra solve in a container of side L = 1 + delta (delta drawn uniformly from [0.02, 0.08] per start) with the centres and radii in that enlarged box, then affinely rescale centres and radii by 1/L back into [0,1]^2 and clip. This lets circles settle in a looser layout and then compresses the whole arrangement, a different route from the radius-scale continuation already on the list. Use the rescaled result as the starting point of the normal phase 2.

title: Gravity compaction post-pass
spec: After each local solve, run a compaction loop of about 200 steps: move every centre a small fraction of the way toward the square centre (0.5, 0.5), step size 0.002 decaying linearly to 0, then resolve any pair overlaps by pushing the two centres apart along their line by half the overlap and re-clipping to the walls. Finally call the usual SLSQP phase 2 once more from the compacted centres. The aim is to pull loose circles into the jammed core so the free-radius solve finds a denser basin. Keep the cost bounded by vectorising the pair update with numpy.

title: Cross-entropy learning of the kick distribution
spec: Treat the kick parameters (centre p, radius R) as a Gaussian distribution that is refit online. Keep a sample set of the last 30 kicks that produced a new best or a sum within 0.002 of the best. At each step, draw the kick centre and radius from a Gaussian fitted to that elite set (mean and covariance of p and R), with a floor on the variance so sampling never collapses, and fall back to the uniform draw during the first 10 steps. Update the elite set after each step. The walk then learns where good kicks land in this packing.

title: Trust-constr polish of the incumbent
spec: Replace the final SLSQP call on the best packing only (not on every start) with scipy.optimize.minimize(method='trust-constr') using the same objective and the same stacked inequality constraints, supplying the analytic sparse Jacobian of the constraints. Run it with gtol 1e-10 and xtol 1e-12 from the best packing, and keep its output only if it is feasible and has a larger radius sum after _repair. This is a different interior-point style local solver used as a finisher, not as a search driver.

title: Radius-entropy annealing in phase 2
spec: Add a term -tau * sum(log(r_i)) to the phase-2 objective, with tau annealed geometrically from 1e-2 to 1e-6 over successive warm-started SLSQP calls (four stages on the same start). At each stage the solver receives the previous output as its start. Keep the constraints identical and take the final stage output for _repair. The aim is to steer the solver through the interior of the radius simplex before the final vertex solution, which is a regularisation of the objective rather than a change of the constraints.

title: Spectral-gap termination with time reallocation
spec: Track the sum of radii after each walk step. When the last 15 steps have improved the best by less than 1e-6 in total, stop the current walk early and start a fresh walk from a new random restart, so unproductive basins do not consume the remaining budget. Count the restart as a new chain of the same walk type. This is a time-allocation rule over the existing kick walk and does not change the local solver or the kick distribution.

title: Differential evolution over centres with SLSQP local refine
spec: On a subset of the time budget, run scipy.optimize.differential_evolution over the 2n centre coordinates. The objective is the sum of radii computed by a fast greedy repair (radius equal to the minimum of the wall distances and half the nearest-neighbour gap), with a penalty for any centre outside the square. Use the seed for the DE random state and a small population. Then take the best centres and run the existing two-phase SLSQP from them. Keep the result only if it beats the random-restart best.

title: Coarse-to-fine radius-scale continuation
spec: Solve first with the radii forced to be at most 0.9 times the wall-gap bound of the final problem, that is, with a shrunken feasible set, then relax the cap to 1.0 in three stages by reusing each stage's solution as the next start. Each stage is a full two-phase SLSQP. The shrunken stages give circles room to settle into a global arrangement before the outer constraints bind. Use the final stage's output as the restart result. This is a continuation over the feasible set, not over the penalty weight, and it has no effect on the validity check, which remains exact.

title: Two-tier tolerance for kick solves
spec: Use a cheap SLSQP for each kick walk step: ftol 1e-5 and maxiter 60. Run the full setting (ftol 1e-10, maxiter 200) only when the cheap result beats the incumbent's sum by more than 1e-4, then keep whichever result is higher after the full solve. This gives each walk many more steps at the cost of a second solve only for promising candidates.

title: Smallest-circle ejection and reinsertion as a kick
spec: As a kick, choose the circle with the smallest radius in the incumbent (ties broken randomly), remove it, and reinsert it at the largest-clearance point found among 500 random samples in the unit square. Set its starting radius to zero, then run the existing two-phase solve. Accept the new packing through the existing best-update rule. This targets the weakest circle directly rather than a random disc of circles.

title: Stagnation-triggered kick escalation
spec: Count consecutive kicks that fail to beat the incumbent. Start the disc radius cap R at 0.2. After every 25 consecutive failures, multiply R by 1.5, capped at 0.6. Reset R to 0.2 whenever the incumbent improves. This replaces the fixed uniform R range in [0.15, 0.35] and needs no extra state beyond two counters.

title: Fixed-size pool of walkers with percentile reseeding
spec: Keep four walkers, each with its own packing and sum. At each step, advance one walker chosen by a softmax over sums with temperature 0.01, applying one kick. Every 50 steps, replace the walker with the lowest sum by a copy of the highest one. Return the best walker at the end. Unlike replica exchange this uses a greedy selection rule and no temperature ladder, so the code stays under twenty lines.

title: Poisson-disc restart with radius-aware spacing
spec: Generate initial centres by dart-throwing Poisson-disc sampling in [0.1, 0.9]^2 with minimum spacing s = 0.9 / sqrt(n) times a random factor in [0.8, 1.1], retrying with smaller spacing until n points are placed. Set the initial radii to half the nearest-neighbour distance, capped at 0.12. Feed this start to the existing equal-radius phase 1. This gives a more even initial spread than uniform sampling, and it is cheap enough to replace one restart in three.

title: Overlap-driven greedy repair instead of radius shrinking
spec: In _repair, when the largest pairwise overlap exceeds 1 percent of the smaller radius, remove the more-overlapped circle and reinsert it at the point with the largest clearance from all other circles among 500 random samples, with its radius set to that clearance. Only fall back to proportional shrinking when the removal loop has run 10 times. This is a structural repair that may keep more total radius than uniform scaling.

title: Quadrant decomposition start
spec: For a random start, split the n circles into four groups sized as evenly as possible (with a random assignment of the remainder). Solve each group as an independent equal-radius packing inside its own quadrant of the unit square, using the phase-1 SLSQP with the quadrant as the container, then use the four solutions as the initial centres and radii for the normal phase 2. The seam between quadrants is then optimised by the global free-radius solve. This is a structured two-level construction rather than a uniform random start.

title: Voronoi-based initial radii
spec: Initialise each circle's radius from the geometry of its random centre instead of a fixed INIT_RADIUS. Compute the Voronoi-like nearest-neighbour distance for each centre (using scipy.spatial.cKDTree on the start centres), then set its initial radius to half the nearest-neighbour distance, capped by the wall distance. Pass this into SLSQP as x0. The start is then nearly feasible from the outset, so SLSQP begins closer to a valid region and may converge in fewer iterations.

title: Fingerprint-deduplicated walk
spec: Compute a fingerprint of each local optimum as the sorted radii rounded to 1e-4, stored in a Python set. If a kicked result returns a fingerprint already seen, do not count it as progress and immediately double the next kick's disc radius for that step. Rejected duplicates cost no further solves. This keeps the walk from cycling among a few basins and needs only a set and one conditional.

title: Minimum-radius tie-break in phase 2
spec: Add a small term to the phase-2 SLSQP objective: minus sum(r) minus 1e-3 times min(r), with min approximated by a smooth softmin over the radii with temperature 1e-3. The tie-break favours packings with more even radii, which often have more room to grow under later kicks. Remove the term in the final polish so the reported value is the true sum of radii.

title: Alternating-projection feasibility pre-step
spec: After the SLSQP phase-1 solve, before phase 2, make the configuration feasible with Dykstra-style alternating projections. Repeat up to 200 times: for each violated pair, push the two centres apart along their connecting line by half the overlap; for each circle crossing a wall, push its centre inward. Keep the radii at the phase-1 value, then compute the maximal feasible radii for these centres with the exact LP already available. Use the resulting radii as the warm start for phase 2. This yields a near-feasible start with a usable radius sum, so SLSQP starts from a feasible point.

title: LP screening of random candidate layouts
spec: Draw K = 30 random centre sets per time slice. For each one, score it cheaply by solving only the radius LP with the centres fixed (linprog, HiGHS, a few milliseconds). Run the full two-phase SLSQP only on the top 2 layouts by LP score, and keep the best final packing. The LP value is a valid lower bound on what the layout can achieve with those centres, so it is a sound filter. Set the number of candidates so that the total time stays inside TIME_FRACTION of the budget.

title: Surrogate-guided kick amplitude
spec: Maintain a log of every kick tried in the walk: its disc centre, radius R, and the resulting change in sum of radii. Every 20 steps, fit a small ridge regression of the improvement on (R, the number of circles inside the disc, the disc centre coordinates) and draw 16 candidate kicks; choose the candidate with the highest predicted improvement with a 20 percent chance of picking a random one instead. Before step 20, use the current uniform kick. This replaces the blind uniform choice with a learned proposal distribution while staying within one solve per step.

title: Constraint-margin annealing
spec: In phase 2, tighten every overlap and wall constraint by a margin delta, so the constraint becomes d_ij - r_i - r_j >= delta and c - r >= delta. Start with delta = 0.01 and solve SLSQP, then halve delta and re-solve from the previous output, down to delta = 0 in about 6 stages. Each stage starts from the last feasible point, so the final stage is the true problem. Repair still runs at the end. The aim is to move the solver through a sequence of interior-feasible points rather than stopping on a boundary-touching point that is slightly infeasible.

title: Local-subproblem solve for kick steps
spec: During the kick walk, after a disc re-randomisation, freeze every circle outside the kick disc and its one-ring of neighbours, and run SLSQP only on the free circles and their radii, with constraints restricted to pairs that involve at least one free circle. Then run one full free-radius SLSQP on the whole packing only if the local result beats the incumbent. The aim is to make each walk step several times cheaper, so the walk gets more steps in the same CPU time. Seeds, kick distribution and repair are otherwise unchanged.

title: Sum-of-powers objective homotopy in phase 2
spec: Replace the phase-2 objective -sum(r) with -sum(r**p), where p starts at 2.0 and is linearly annealed to 1.0 over the phase-2 SLSQP calls in a walk (for example, each call uses the p value for its position in the walk). The exponent p>1 favours uneven radii early and the final p=1 solves the true problem, which may move the optimiser through different basins. Use the analytic gradient 2*p*r**(p-1) on the radius block or a finite difference. Keep phase 1 unchanged.

title: Tabu-diversified kick centres
spec: Keep a list of the centres of the last 10 kicks. When choosing a new kick centre p, draw 20 candidate uniform points and keep the one farthest from every tabu centre (minimum-distance criterion), instead of a plain uniform draw. Expire tabu entries after 10 steps. This pushes the walk to perturb regions it has not recently disturbed, without changing the kick radius or the acceptance rule.

title: Phase-1 score as a cheap gate for phase 2
spec: Run only phase 1 (equal-radius SLSQP) on each kick candidate, which is cheap. Compute the common radius t it reaches and run the full free-radius phase 2 only if t exceeds 0.99 times the best t seen so far for the incumbent walk. Otherwise discard the candidate without a phase-2 solve. The gate is scale-free and uses the existing phase-1 result, so it adds no new objective or constraint. Calibrate the 0.99 factor once against the incumbent.

title: Radius-only multiplicative kick
spec: As an alternative kick on some steps (for example one step in three), leave every centre unchanged and multiply the radii of a random 30 percent of the circles by factors drawn uniformly from [0.5, 1.0]. Then run only the free-radius phase-2 SLSQP starting from these centres and shrunken radii. This moves the optimiser through the radius-allocation landscape without disturbing the geometry, which the centre-kick family does not explore.

title: Mirror-symmetric reduced parameterisation for the first start
spec: For the first random start only, optimise in a reduced space where circles come in mirror pairs across the vertical line x=0.5 (about n/2 free centres plus one centre on the line if n is odd, with radii paired). Run phase 1 and a phase-2 SLSQP in this reduced space, which has roughly half the variables and constraints, then unfold to the full 26 circles and run the existing free-radius phase-2 SLSQP on the full problem to polish. Keep the rest of the walk unchanged. This differs from the earlier symmetric initial configuration idea, because the symmetry is enforced during the optimisation and not only used to seed it.

title: Symmetric paired kicks across the diagonal
spec: On each kick, choose a random circle i and its mirror image j under the reflection (x, y) -> (y, x) of the current incumbent, which is a symmetry of the square. Perturb the disc of radius R around c_i and the disc around c_j at the same time, using the same random displacements, mirrored. Re-optimise as usual. Mirror-coupled kicks explore the symmetric-looking region of the configuration space, which the random single-disc kick rarely reaches, and they cost no extra solver time.

title: Random-angle lattice slice start
spec: For each start, choose a random rotation angle and a random lattice spacing such that about n lattice points fall in the square. Take the n points closest to the square centre as initial centres, perturb them by small Gaussian noise (sd 0.01), and run the existing phase 2 SLSQP with radii set from the nearest-neighbour distance. This changes only the initial configuration and uses the seed for the angle and spacing, so each restart explores a different lattice orientation.

title: Bottom-left-fill greedy start
spec: For each start, draw target radii from a random profile (sorted descending), then place circles one at a time in order of decreasing radius. Each circle goes to the lowest, then leftmost, candidate point on a grid of about 400 points plus tangency points against already placed circles, where it fits inside the square without overlap. Circles that cannot be placed get a tiny radius. The result is the start for the free-radius phase 2 SLSQP, which skips phase 1 for that start. Keep the existing walk and repair unchanged.

title: Subset-first curriculum solve
spec: On each random start, solve the packing for a random subset of about 80 percent of the circles from scratch with the existing two-phase SLSQP. Then insert the remaining circles at the largest empty holes of that packing, and run phase 2 on all circles. The subset is chosen by the seed. Differs from largest-hole insertion from the best n-1 packing because the subset is solved first, from random centres, as a full problem.

title: Half-plane reflection kick
spec: Replace the disc re-randomisation kick with a reflection kick. Pick a random line through a random point in the square with a random direction. Reflect the centres on one side of the line across it, clip to [0,1], and set the radii of the reflected circles to zero before re-optimising with the existing two-phase SLSQP. Circles on the other side stay put. Acceptance stays strict-improvement and the walk keeps its current structure.

title: Riesz-energy homotopy start
spec: Before phase 1, place centres by minimising the Riesz energy sum over pairs of 1/d^s with L-BFGS-B. Anneal the exponent s from 1 to 12 in five stages, with random initial centres and the square as bounds. The energy law is different from soft-repulsion and Langevin annealing: it drives centres apart with a power law rather than a penalty. Hand the final centres to the existing phase 1 SLSQP to set the radii. Keep the code to one helper function.

title: Frozen-small-circle start
spec: On each random start, choose k of the circles (k from 2 to 5, chosen by the seed) to be small. Fix their radii at 0.02 for the first solve, optimise the rest with SLSQP, then release all radii and run the existing phase 2 SLSQP. This makes the optimiser place the large circles first, which may create open gaps that the small circles then fill. The walk logic is unchanged.

title: Max-min-distance point-spreading start
spec: For the first random start, first solve the max-min-distance problem for n points in the unit square: maximise t subject to pairwise squared distances at least t and each point in [0,1]^2, using SLSQP with an epigraph variable and a random initial point. Set each radius to half its nearest-neighbour distance, capped by the wall distance, and use this as the start for phase 2. This replaces the equal-radius phase 1 for that start only. Seeds are used for all randomness.

title: Two-level cluster packing
spec: On each random start, split the n circles into k groups of about 3 to 5 using a seeded k-means on random initial centres. Pack each group as one super-circle with SLSQP (the group's radius is the sum of its members' radii plus the enclosing margin), then pack the super-circles in the square. Expand each group by scaling its members into its disc and run the existing full two-phase SLSQP on all circles. This is a hierarchical start that is structurally different from the size-class stagewise idea.
